correctness.rationale: The map ν:P¹×P^{m−1}×P^{n−1}→R_{m,n} taking (ℓ,F,G)↦(ℓF,ℓG) is proper with finite fibers (common roots), generically one-to-one and source smooth, hence normalization. Its residual resultant D is the irreducible Cartier divisor class (0,n−1,m−1) and full preimage of S₂, the degree≥2 common factor locus. Hypersurface adjunction gives ν*ω_R=O_N(−2,n−m−1,m−n−1) while ω_N=O_N(−2,−m,−n), so finite duality yields conductor invertible ideal sheaf O_N(0,1−n,1−m). The conductor support is irreducible D; effective multiplicity forced exactly one by Pic(N)=Z³, so conductor ideal I_D and radical downstairs contraction is I_{S₂,red}. The Euler polynomial follows from 0→O_R→ν*O_N→Q→0 and bidegree(n,m) hypersurface exact sequence, valid for all integer twists via generalized binomials. Independent symbolic Pic/class and low-degree Euler checks verified sample degrees. Full all-degree argument depends on accepted finite duality and support criterion; finite checker is not proof.

originality.rationale: Choudary 1990 proves the normalization map and singular/gcd strata, including generic normal crossings, and is fully credited. Its original five-page primary paper does not supply the global multiplicity-one conductor ideal or normalization-defect two-variable Euler polynomial. General duality supplies a tool but not the specific divisor identification. Eisenbud–Schreyer–Weyman arXiv:math/0111040 addresses Chow complexes/determinantal resultants and does not directly compute this normalization defect. A historical elimination-theoretic conductor formula could be unindexed.
residual_risks: A classical elimination-theory conductor ideal formula not indexed by modern keywords may establish stronger priority coverage.
Uses characteristic zero, m,n≥2, projective product polarization; does not compute Jacobian scheme or all higher-gcd analytic germs.
Ancillary Eisenbud–Schreyer paper was not material-read in full, so no whole-document negative claim is made.

value.rationale: The exact reduced conductor distinguishes scheme-theoretic normalization defect from the Jacobian ideal and determines its multiplicity at all higher-gcd strata uniformly in m,n. The full bigraded Euler polynomial is a natural exact invariant of these nonnormal resultant hypersurfaces and useful for adjunction and sheaf calculations, not a single narrow numerical slice.
